title: Pars III opens: two questions Rome still presses against Scripture sufficiency
source_text: I. TOTA haec controversia ad duo referri potest, quae, quanquam valde connexa sunt, distingui tamen debent. Unum est an omnia quae necessaria sunt ad fidem & religionem plene & sufficienter in Scriptura contineantur. Alterum an praeter Scripturam sit in Ecclesia quoddam aliud Dei verbum paris cum Scriptura sacra authoritatis, quod traditione non scripta ad nos derivatum sit. Prius negant Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, posterius affirmant, & suam, circa utrumque, sententiam multis argumentis confirmare conantur.
pass_a_gloss: This whole controversy can be referred to two points, which, though tightly connected, must nevertheless be distinguished. One is whether all things necessary to faith and religion are contained fully and sufficiently in Scripture. The other is whether, besides Scripture, there is in the Church some other word of God of equal authority with sacred Scripture, derived to us by unwritten tradition. The doctors of the Roman Church deny the former and affirm the latter, and try to confirm their opinion on both points with many arguments.
pass_b_english: Pars III opens by splitting the fight into two questions that travel together but are not the same.
First: are all things necessary to faith and religion fully and sufficiently in Scripture?
Second: is there, beside Scripture, another word of God in the Church, equal in authority, handed down only by unwritten tradition?
Rome denies the first and affirms the second, and piles arguments on both.

lemmas.gloss: of equal authority with sacred Scripture

choices.english: equal in authority with sacred Scripture
